risks.risk: Wrong fitment (different gearbox variant for the claimed Ford model/engine, or wrong drive configuration). Photos don’t show the gearbox code/part number.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear close-up photo of the gearbox identification plate/label (part number + gearbox code) and the transmission tag, plus the vehicle application it came from.

risks.risk: Not actually tested/working (could have internal faults not visible in photos).
risks.proof: Ask for a short video of the gearbox being tested (engaged in gear / reverse) or a mechanic’s test sheet with date and results.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst-case: not working / needs overhaul.

risks.risk: Condition issues (leaks, missing sensors/solenoids, damaged harness connectors) that photos may not fully reveal.
risks.proof: Ask for photos of all ports/connectors, fluid drain/fill areas, and any sensor/solenoid locations; plus a checklist of included parts.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst-case: may be missing/needs parts.

risks.risk: Drive type mismatch (e.g., 4x4 vs 2WD, pin count, or transfer case compatibility).
risks.proof: Ask for the gearbox pin count/variant info from the label and a photo showing the transfer/drive interface (if applicable).

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the gearbox identification plate/label showing part number + gearbox code (photo 0/1/2: request tighter shots where the label is).
Video proof of testing: gearbox engaged (forward/reverse) and any diagnostic readout if available.
Photo of all connectors/sensors/ports and what exactly is included (starter/torque converter/hoses/solenoids if applicable).
State the exact transmission variant details (drive type, pin count, and whether it’s for 2WD/4WD) matching the label.
